A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of trained diagonal and quadratic networks, including learning curves, weight spectra, and regularization sensitivity in Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and adds noiseless learning curves for both architectures in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The architectures, regularized ERM objectives, and training procedures are retained. However, v1's post-training spectral pruning estimator, defined in Corollary 2 and analyzed in Appendix C.5, is removed rather than relocated.

E1.justification: Figure 5 adds a noiseless teacher-student scenario with label-noise variance zero. Coverage otherwise remains synthetic Gaussian regression with power-law teachers and the same two network architectures.

E2.justification: The experimental comparisons retain trained networks versus state-evolution predictions. Appendix E introduces an analytical comparison with ridge regression, but no ridge experiment or other empirical comparator is added.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes the reported metric to normalized excess risk, rescaled to start at one. The new Figure 5 explicitly inherits Figure 3's dimensions and regularization settings while setting noise to zero. These changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 5 provides a controlled removal of label noise relative to Figure 3, testing the predicted changes in scaling and overfitting behavior. Existing spectral analyses and regularization-sensitivity experiments are retained as Figures 6–8.

E5.justification: Both numerical appendices report approximately ten Monte Carlo matrix samples per order parameter and iteration. Neither version adds experimental seed counts, repeated-training summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The new Figure 5 supplies systematic noiseless learning curves for both architectures, supporting faster decay and the disappearance of the noisy interpolation peak. These are additional results under different noise conditions, not same-setting performance improvements. Existing spectrum and sensitivity plots are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds noiseless rates and optimality results in Appendix B, corresponding derivations in Appendices C and D.5, and the ridge-regression theorem in Appendix E. Appendix D.3 adds substantial boundary-layer derivations. The pruning corollary and proof are removed. The new Equation (279) has an exponent inconsistent with the noiseless optimality corollary.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions remain essentially unchanged. Section 1.2 broadens the explicit scope from noisy ERM to nonnegative noise, supported by the new noiseless results, while retaining the central universality and spectra–generalization claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the description of discontinuous rates with a narrow boundary-layer interpretation. Section 2.3 removes the pruning-based argument that learned features can simply be separated from noise and adds a distinction between phases VIa and VIb regarding Bayes optimality. Appendix B explains the simpler noiseless spectral behavior.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the regularization rescaling in the network-to-matrix mapping and explains normalization differences between the main presentation and derivations in Appendix D.1. The code access information, LBFGS implementation, convergence precision, hardware, and reported computing cost are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds connections to Worschech and Rosenow, Kothapalli et al., and Martin and Hinrichs, among others. Pruning-related references are removed with that discussion. Publication updates for existing works do not represent new citations or comparators.

P1.justification: The quadratic ERM derivation is substantially rewritten and reorganized around common calculations followed by overregularized and underregularized phases. The perturbative expansion is integrated into the Bayesian derivation, diagonal conjecture material is consolidated in the appendix, and noisy and noiseless derivations are separated. The main narrative receives lighter editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds the noiseless phase diagram and simulation panels as Figures 4 and 5, updates Figure 1's annotations and caption, and normalizes Figure 3's axes. Original Figures 4–6 become Figures 6–8 with unchanged plots; the overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: The noiseless simulations broaden empirical support, while the boundary-layer analysis and ridge comparison improve interpretation of the framework. The net gain is limited by removal of the pruning extension and inconsistencies in the added mathematics: Equation (279) states (n/d)^(2γ−1), opposite to Appendix B's (n/d)^(1−2γ). The central non-asymptotic justification also remains conjectural.
